options: A sector-specific group where companies share incident reports
A type of firewall that blocks malicious IPs automatically
An antivirus engine that scans files for known signatures
A standardized, JSON-based format for describing threat intelligence in detail, including threat actors, campaigns, and indicators
questions.explain: STIX (Structured Threat Information eXpression) describes threat intel in a structured way so it means the same thing across different organizations' tools.

questions.q: What does TAXII provide that STIX does not?
options: A scoring system for how dangerous a threat actor is
The actual malware samples referenced in an IOC
A list of approved antivirus vendors
The transport protocol — an HTTPS-based API for physically moving STIX data between organizations
questions.explain: STIX describes what is being shared; TAXII defines how it moves, through TAXII servers hosting collections and TAXII clients pulling or subscribing to them.

questions.q: Why are STIX and TAXII almost always discussed and deployed together?
options: Because TAXII cannot function unless STIX is uninstalled first
They were designed as a pair specifically to solve automated threat-intel sharing, and that pairing is now the real industry standard
Because regulations only allow them to be used in combination
Because they are actually two names for the exact same standard
questions.explain: The two standards complement each other — one for data format, one for transport — and together they're the pairing used by programs like CISA's AIS and platforms like MISP.

options: A type of malware sample repository
A firewall rule set unrelated to threat intelligence
A list of employees with access to a SIEM
A bundle of STIX data on a given topic, hosted on a TAXII server
questions.explain: A TAXII server hosts one or more collections, each a bundle of STIX content on a particular topic, which TAXII clients can pull from or subscribe to.

questions.q: In the lesson's example, how does Company B's firewall end up updated with new IOCs before its own analysts finish investigating a shared attack campaign?
options: Company B's analysts manually copy the IOCs from a phone call with Company A
The firewall updates itself on a fixed weekly schedule unrelated to any feed
Company A directly logs into Company B's firewall to make the change
Company B's TIP is subscribed to the ISAC's TAXII collection and automatically pulls the STIX bundle Company A published, then pushes the new IOCs out
questions.explain: Because Company B's TIP is already subscribed to that TAXII collection, the STIX bundle Company A published arrives and gets enforced automatically, with no manual step required.
